title: OTA, partitions, and rollback

spans.text: Goal: apply “OTA, partitions, and rollback” to a real program or device. The key principle is: Rollback provides a path back to a known-good image. In a project, follow this guidance: Test update recovery under power loss, poor connectivity, and incompatible versions.
QUESTION: What will this example do? Predict the result first.
Safe only after authenticity and compatibility checks; partition layout and recovery behavior are project-specific.

OTA can write firmware to an inactive partition. Design partition layout, image size, signature/version checks, health confirmation, and rollback together.

This example calls the ESP-IDF OTA partition API from an Arduino-ESP32 sketch. Partition selection, rollback, and signature verification are not generic Arduino APIs. ArduinoOTA/Update can support simpler update flows, but secure rollback needs explicit ESP-IDF partition and verification configuration.

Key line: `esp_ota_mark_app_valid_cancel_rollback();`
What it does: Rollback provides a path back to a known-good image.
Why it is used: Test update recovery under power loss, poor connectivity, and incompatible versions.
If omitted or changed: Do not boot an OTA image before validating its signature.
